core_obligations: Part (1), setup (proof lines 1088-1093): with e : ker(f) -> ker(k) induced by g and i, j the canonical injections, cartesianness supplies t : ker(k) -> w with f t = 0 and g t = j, hence a morphism u : ker(k) -> ker(f) with i u = t.

Part (1), the two inverse relations (proof lines 1094-1100): the computations g i u e = g t e = j e = g i and f i u e = 0 = f i give i u e = i, so u e is the identity after cancelling the monomorphism i; and j e u = g i u = g t = j gives e u = the identity after cancelling the monomorphism j.
Part (2) (proof line 1101): the statement about cokernels of a cocartesian square follows by duality.
proof_roadmap: Use cartesianness to produce a morphism from the kernel of the lower horizontal map.
Factor that morphism through the kernel of the upper horizontal map.
Cancel the two kernel injections to get the two inverse relations, and dualize.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that in a commutative square in an abelian category, cartesianness makes the induced map between the kernels of the two horizontal maps an isomorphism, and dually for cokernels and cocartesian squares (statement lines 1068-1086). The proof is a complete argument for the first assertion: cartesianness provides a morphism into the upper left object which factors through the kernel of the upper horizontal map (proof lines 1088-1093), and two displayed computations in which the kernel injections are cancelled give the two inverse relations (proof lines 1094-1100); the second assertion follows by duality. The non-formal content is the construction of the morphism from the kernel and the two cancellations. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
